title: BA1/508/2021 of TRILOK SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 508 of 2021
Trilok Singh ...Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ....Respondent
Present:-
Mr. S.K. Mandal, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. S.S. Adhikari, Deputy Advocate General with Ms. Lata Negi, Brief Holder for
the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Applicant Trilok Singh is in judicial custody in FIR No.
152 of 2018, under Section 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B IPC, Police
Station Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar. He has sought his
release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. In the year 2011, a person Satya Singh got sanctioned a
loan of Rs. 7,00,000/- for agricultural purposes. The co-accused
identified him and stood guarantor for the loan. The loan was not repaid.
When the bank officials visited the village in the year 2016, they came to
know that there is no person named Satya Singh in the village, instead
the photograph which was there on the loan document, that was of the
applicant Trilok Singh. It is thereafter an FIR was lodged.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would argue that in fact
the applicant is Satya Singh and not Trilok Singh. He has been arrested
as Trilok Singh. He has all the identity proof as Satya Singh, which he
had produced while taking loan. He was identified as Satya Singh by the
guarantor as well as the bank officials. Reference has been made to the
statement of Kamaljeet Singh, the Field Officer, who sanctioned the
loan, in which he has stated that at the time of sanctioning of the loan he

2
visited the village and the neighbours and other people around identified
the applicant as Satya Singh. It is also argued that there is no other
person named Satya Singh. Nobody has come up to claim that he is
Satya Singh. The applicant is in possession of all the land, which is
recorded in his name as Satya Singh, therefore it is a case fit for bail.
5. Learned State Counsel would submit that, in fact, the
Village Pradhan has identified, based on the photograph, that the
applicant is Trilok Singh and not Satya Singh. He forged the identify
proof of Satya Singh by replacing his photograph and took the loan. It is
a case of forgery.
6. Be that as it may, it is a case of identity. Applicant claims
that he is Satya Singh and he took loan as such, and he was identified by
the neighbours after verification by the Field Officer of the bank. He has
all documents with regard to his identity.
7. Who issued identity card in favour of the applicant or Satya
Singh? Where are the original records, in which the photograph of Satya
Singh was replaced by the applicant? This record is not before this Court
at this moment. Perhaps they would be deliberated during trial.
8. Having considered, this Court is of the view that it is a case
fit for bail and the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
9. The bail application is allowed.
10. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a
personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like
amount, to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
11. This bail order be forwarded to concerned Court as well as
the concerned jail through e-mail also.
